items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training
Advanced degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training
Minimum of 4-7 years of experience in conduct administration and or student services
Previous experience working with student conduct issues in a university setting
Experience in managing and meeting simultaneous needs of multiple clients.
Experience working with college students
Experience with a conduct management database

Case Management: Responsible for interpreting organization policies and advising students and faculty on student conduct, student grievances, disputes, and issues regarding discrimination. Reviews and resolves 200-300 academic and social misconduct violations by students annually. Refers and presents cases to the Student Conduct and Academic Integrity Committees. Develops, implements, and monitors developmentally appropriate educational sanctions. Collects and analyzes data and prepares reports as needed, including Clery Act and other agency requests. Maintains records and files of disciplinary cases in keeping with applicable University policies and state/federal laws. (40% time)

Perform service in one or more of the following major program areas: 1) Conduct Committee Coordination: serves as primary coordinator for hearing committees, including recruitment and training of faculty, staff, and student committee members and scheduling of hearings; 2) Academic Integrity Programs Coordination: coordinates Academic Integrity Seminar including recruitment, training, and scheduling of peer facilitators; 3) Student Organization Case Coordination: serves as primary case manager for referrals involving student organizations; acts as liaison between Student Conduct & Academic Integrity Programs and Student Life; 4) Residential Education Conduct Coordination: serves as case manager for cases involving residential students; 5) OCR hearing coordination: coordinates hearings and manages cases under SVSH and Anti-Discrimination Policies. (20% time)

Case Intake and Coordination: Provide primary case intake functions including walk-ins, calls, and department email, providing accurate and courteous responses to faculty and students. Maintain calendar and schedule appointments and hearings; anticipate potential conflicts and suggest alternatives. Manage Office of Civil Rights (OCR) cases (including SVSH and Anti-Discrimination cases) and coordinate related hearings. Assist with all types of student hearing committee scheduling. Compose, draft, edit, and finalize correspondence and other documents/spreadsheets using Microsoft Office applications and Symplicity Advocate. Review and update policy and procedural information, including making edits on the department website. Coordinate and maintain emergency response plan and equipment for department, and emergency and routine maintenance service for all department facilities. Assist with hiring and training new employees. Compile and redact records for authorized releases. Coordinate daily office operations with a focus on providing superior customer service. Provide routine reports from Advocate in support of the student conduct process. (15% time)

Conduct Database Management: Assist with the processing of new incidents into the Advocate conduct database, including accurate details and uploading supporting documents for academic, social and OCR cases. Enter academic and social misconduct reports into the case management program. Contact instructors and/or other reporting parties when further documentation is required. Refer cases and related documents to OCR through OCR's online reporting system, for their review and possible investigation. Receive, review, and upload student sanction assignments along with other related notices to the case management database. (10% time)
Plans, designs, and provides workshops for students, such as information about the organization, or academic strategies and enrichment programs. (5% time)
Other duties as necessary (5% time)
Supervises student staff (5% time)
Read/Comprehend: Constantly
Write: Constantly
Perform Calculations: Occasionally
Communicate Orally: Constantly
Reason & Analyze: Constantly
Sit: Constantly

Ability to handle restricted and sensitive information in accordance with federal and state laws and University polices. Ability to maintain high levels of confidentiality, attention to detail, accuracy, and a commitment to University ethical principles in all areas of responsibility.
Knowledge of and ability to work within a comprehensive student conduct database, and knowledge of University-specific computer application programs.
Multicultural competencies; ability to work with diverse populations, and with sensitive information related to protected classes.
Working knowledge of student development theory, UC policies and procedures, state/federal law, and laws related to student privacy such as FERPA, related to the responsibilities of the position.

Excellent written and oral communication skills, using tact and diplomacy in an environment focused on customer service. Ability to produce a high volume and quality of written correspondence and investigative information.
Working knowledge of advising and counseling techniques.

Interpersonal skills including conflict resolution, mediation, and problem solving skills to resolve complex, multifaceted, and often emotionally-charged disputes and to assist parties in reaching resolution..
Strong organizational and time management skills, ability to set priorities, balance a heavy workload, adhere to a schedule and meet deadlines.
